rules.title: AB 325 Cartwright Act: Common Pricing Algorithm Restrictions
rules.requirement: The Cartwright Act prohibits using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade or coerce users into adopting pricing recommendations.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies generally to persons using or distributing common pricing algorithms to restrain trade or coerce prices.

rules.exemptions: Does not include the end consumer of a product or service.
rules.citation: AB-325 / Business and Professions Code Section 16729
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
(b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.

rules.title: California Tenant Screening Fee Limits and Requirements
rules.requirement: The maximum tenant screening fee a landlord can charge a prospective tenant is capped at $68.96 for 2026, and landlords cannot charge a fee if no unit is available.

coverage_conditions.summary: Prospective tenants applying for residential rental units in California.

rules.quoted_span:
The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
$68.96

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination
rules.requirement: Under the California Tenant Protection Act, landlords cannot terminate a residential tenancy without just cause after 12 months of continuous occupancy, and must provide relocation assistance equal to one month's rent for no-fault evictions.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential real property after 12 or 24 months of continuous occupancy, excluding hotels, institutional housing, certain owner-occupied properties, housing less than 15 years old, separately alienable properties under specific non-corporate ownership, and deed-restricted affordable housing.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts certain single-family owner-occupied residences, owner-occupied duplexes, and non-corporate separately alienable properties meeting statutory ownership and notice requirements.
coverage_conditions.unresolvable: Tenancy duration and specific ownership corporate structures require facts beyond a simple address record.

rules.exemptions: Transient occupancy, nonprofit/religious/extended care/residential care facilities, dormitories, shared bathroom/kitchen with owner, certain single-family owner-occupied residences (including ADUs/JADUs or mobilehomes), owner-occupied two-unit structures, housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, certain separately alienable properties (not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member) with proper notice, and deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.
rules.interaction: May preempt the listed local rules once in force; every affected address is flagged for human review rather than decided.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.conflict_note: possible preemption of r-0009 (Berkeley, CA), r-0014 (Los Angeles, CA), r-0018 (San Diego, CA), r-0020 (San Francisco, CA), r-0023 (Santa Ana, CA)

rules.title: Statewide Rent Increase Limits
rules.requirement: Statewide rent increases are capped at 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period.
rules.key_value: 5% plus cost of living or 10% max

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential real property statewide, excluding government-subsidized housing, dormitories, housing subject to stricter local rent control, units issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, certain separately alienable properties without corporate/REIT ownership, and certain owner-occupied duplexes.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts certain separately alienable properties (like single-family homes or condos) owned by individuals rather than corporations, REITs, or LLCs with corporate members, and owner-occupied duplexes.

rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted affordable housing, dormitories, stricter local rent control housing, units built within the last 15 years, certain independently alienable properties not owned by corporations/REITs/certain LLCs, and owner-occupied duplexes.
rules.interaction: Yields to stricter local law: where a listed local rule covers the unit, the local rule governs and this one is reported as superseded.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rules.title: Fair Employment and Housing Act Protected Characteristics
rules.requirement: The Fair Employment and Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on a broad list of protected characteristics and source of income, and restricts criminal history inquiries by banning blanket bans and unconvicted arrests.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to most housing accommodations and providers in California.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: When an owner is occupying a home and is renting to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics, though they still cannot make discriminatory advertisements.

rules.exemptions: When an owner is occupying a home and is renting to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics (except for advertising). Senior housing and homeless youth housing may also be limited based on age under specific statutory requirements.
rules.quoted_span:
The Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) covers the sale, rental, or occupancy of most housing accommodations in California, including single-family homes, multi-family homes, condominiums, apartments, short-term rentals, mobile homes, subsidized housing, dormitories, sober living facilities,  group homes, residential motels,
emergency shelters, homeless shelters, shelters for survivors of domestic violence
, recreational vehicles (RVs) used as a home, farmworker housing, and boats used as homes

rules.title: Security Deposit Limit
rules.requirement: Landlords may generally charge up to one month's rent for a security deposit (two months for qualifying small landlords owning two or fewer properties with up to four units) and must return deposits within 21 days with itemized deductions.

coverage_conditions.summary: Most residential rental units, with exemptions for certain small landlords.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts landlords who own no more than two rental properties with a total of no more than four residential units.

rules.exemptions: Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC where all members are natural persons.
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

rules.title: Prohibition on Coordinated Pricing Algorithms
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy levels, and vendors are prohibited from selling or providing such algorithms to landlords in Berkeley.

coverage_conditions.summary: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.exemptions: Excludes products that publish aggregated and anonymous rental data without recommending terms, products used to set rent/income limits under affordable housing guidelines, and data used strictly for financing research, appraisals, or software development and testing.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Prohibition of Non-Refundable Application Fees for Existing Tenancies
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee for lease renewals or roommate changes, and when charging screening fees, must provide a disclosure statement of applicant rights and the maximum fee cap.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential rental properties in Berkeley when an applicant requests to rent and a fee is charged.

rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rules.title: 2026 Relocation Assistance Payments for Owner Move-In and Ellis Act Evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords executing owner move-in or Ellis Act evictions must pay a standard relocation assistance payment of $19,413, plus an additional $6,471 for qualifying households.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to units subject to owner move-in or Ellis Act evictions under the Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance and Ellis Implementation Ordinance.
coverage_conditions.unresolvable: Relocation requirements apply specifically to owner move-in and Ellis Act evictions.

rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; Ellis Implementation Ordinance
rules.quoted_span:
The standard relocation assistance payment will increase to
$19,413
.
The additional relocation assistance payment for qualifying households will increase to
$6,47
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0003 (California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination) from 2024-04-01

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment Maximum Cap
rules.requirement: The Annual General Adjustment (AGA) for fully covered rental units is capped at a maximum of 5% per year, overriding higher calculation formulas.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to fully covered rental units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.

rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: The Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits landlords from asking about, requiring disclosure of, or considering criminal history in rental advertising, applications, or tenant selection, with specific exemptions such as owner-occupied properties with 1 to 3 units.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential rental housing in Berkeley with specific exemptions for lifetime sex offenders, certain public housing/Section 8 properties, and owner-occupied properties with 1 to 3 units.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Owner-occupied properties between 1-3 units in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence.

rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied 1-3 unit properties; units under agreements allowing owner move-in under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest
rules.requirement: Landlords of units covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance must pay tenants annual or prorated interest on their security deposits, while adhering to general state deposit limits and return timelines.

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
coverage_conditions.unresolvable: Whether the unit is fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance

rules.exemptions: Units not covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

rules.title: Instruction to Report on Algorithm-Based Rent Setting Ban
rules.requirement: A pending city council motion instructs the Los Angeles Housing Department to report on algorithm-based software usage for establishing rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban.

coverage_conditions.summary: Citywide rental housing

rules.quoted_span:
I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to 
report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based 
software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of this software to set 
rents in the City.

rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: The Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance prohibits terminations without just cause, mandates relocation assistance for no-fault evictions, and requires rental debt to exceed the Fair Market Rent threshold for nonpayment evictions.

coverage_conditions.summary: Covers most residential properties in Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO, after a 6-month residency or lease expiration.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exemptions include owner's roommate and certain properties owned by HACLA or the government.
coverage_conditions.unresolvable: Tenant length of residency (at least six months) or lease expiration required.

rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term substance abuse treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government.
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0003 (California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination) from 2024-04-01

rules.title: Annual Allowable Rent Increase for RSO Units (2025-2026)
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases for RSO units are capped at 3% from July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026, and landlords are prohibited from adding utility percentage increases starting February 2, 2026.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, and specified types including apartments, condos/townhomes under specific tenancy dates, duplexes, multiple single-family units on a parcel, and others.

rules.exemptions: Non-RSO properties are exempt from this specific limit and are subject to separate guidelines.
rules.quoted_span:
Annual rent increases for rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), effective
July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026
is
3%

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest Requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords of properties subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance must pay interest on security deposits monthly or annually via direct payment or rent credit after written notice.

coverage_conditions.summary: Properties subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (LARSO).
coverage_conditions.unresolvable: Applies to properties subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (LARSO).

rules.quoted_span: Interest shall begin accruing on November 1, 1990, on a monthly basis. A tenant shall be given the unpaid accrued interest in the form of either a direct payment or a credit against the tenant’s rent. The landlord shall choose between these two methods of payment and notify the tenant in writing of his or her choice.

rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from terminating a residential rental tenancy without at-fault or no-fault just cause, with specific exemptions for recent construction and certain properties.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential rental properties in San Diego with several standard exemptions including units less than 15 years old, certain single-family homes, and government-subsidized affordable housing.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts certain single-family residences occupied by the landlord or properties where the landlord shares a kitchen/bathroom or owns specific separate dwelling units.

rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels, short-term rentals, deed-restricted affordable housing, mobilehomes under Mobilehome Residency Law, hospitals/care facilities, university dorms, units sharing kitchen/bath with landlord, single-family homes with limited rooms/ADUs rented, owner-occupied duplexes, housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years, and certain separately alienable properties owned by natural persons.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0003 (California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination) from 2024-04-01

rules.title: Prohibition of Algorithmic Devices for Rent Setting
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using software or algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rental prices or manage occupancy levels for residential units.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential units in San Francisco.

rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

rules.title: Just Cause Requirement for Evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords must have one of 17 permitted just cause reasons to evict a tenant from a unit covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance.

coverage_conditions.summary: Covers rental units subject to the Rent Ordinance, including units exempt from rent increases such as those built after June 13, 1979.

rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0003 (California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination) from 2024-04-01

rules.title: Annual Allowable Rent Increase for 2026-2027
rules.requirement: The annual allowable rent increase for rent-controlled units in San Francisco is set to 1.6% from March 1, 2026, through February 28, 2027.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to rent-controlled units in San Francisco.

rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest Rate
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on residential security deposits at the rate of 4.2% for the period from March 1, 2026, to February 28, 2027.

coverage_conditions.summary: Covered residential security deposits in San Francisco.

rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Board Current Rates
rules.quoted_span: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.title: Just Cause for Eviction and Relocation Assistance
rules.requirement: Landlords must have just cause to terminate a tenancy after 30 days and must provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive 3 months of rent for no-fault evictions.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential properties after 30 days, with specific exclusions such as housing produced in the last 15 years and deed-restricted affordable housing.

rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.

rules.title: Maximum Rent Increase Limit
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are capped at the lower of 3% per year or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change over the most recent 12-month period.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential buildings, excluding those constructed after February 1, 1995, and mobile home spaces offered after January 1, 1990.

rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from charging prospective tenants application fees or any upfront charges besides first month's rent, last month's rent, security deposit, and lock-change fees. Any real estate broker finding fee must be paid exclusively by the party who originally engaged the broker.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to lessors/landlords statewide.

rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Notice to determine estate at will and cure for nonpayment
rules.requirement: For tenancies at will, landlords must provide a 14-day written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent with a 10-day cure period. Additionally, landlords are prohibited from taking reprisals against tenants for reporting code violations or joining tenant unions.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to estates at will.

rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy; provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due.

rules.title: General prohibition on rent control with voluntary exception
rules.requirement: Cities and towns are generally prohibited from enacting, maintaining, or enforcing rent control, except that municipalities accepting the chapter may adopt a voluntary rent control system where compliance by property owners is entirely optional and uncoerced.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to rental units unless owned by a person or entity owning less than ten units or having a fair market rent exceeding $400.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Exempts units owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units.

rules.exemptions: Rental units owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units or having a fair market rent exceeding $400.

rules.requirement: It is unlawful for housing owners, lessors, brokers, or managing agents to discriminate in rental, sale, financing, or terms based on protected characteristics including race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, ancestry, genetic information, handicap, children, or receipt of public assistance or housing subsidies.

rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.

rules.title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Rent Control Exemption
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to newly constructed multiple dwellings.

rules.interaction: May preempt the listed local rules once in force; every affected address is flagged for human review rather than decided.
rules.quoted_span:
Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly 
constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period 
of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.conflict_note: possible preemption of r-0044 (Jersey City, NJ)

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Criminal Record Screening Limitations
rules.requirement: Housing providers are prohibited from inquiring about or considering an applicant's criminal record prior to issuing a conditional offer of rental housing, with limited exceptions.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to rental dwelling units in New Jersey, excluding dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are exempt

rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.quoted_span:
A
housing provider
shall not require an applicant to
complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an
applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer,
except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been
convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production
of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether
the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State
sex offender registration program.

rules.title: Maximum Security Deposit Limit
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from charging a security deposit exceeding one and one-half times one month's rent, and must return the deposit within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, excluding owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless requested by tenant.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless tenant requests application of the law.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Exemption for 1-4 Unit Properties
rules.requirement: All 1 to 4 unit residential properties are exempt from Jersey City's rent control regulations.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential properties; 1-4 unit properties are exempt.

rules.exemptions: Properties with 1 to 4 units are exempt.
rules.citation: Chapter 260 of the Jersey City Municipal Code
rules.quoted_span: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control
rules.conflict_note: may be preempted by r-0041 (Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Rent Control Exemption) from None
